\\\"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\\\",\\n  \\\"payload_sha256\\\": \\\"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\\\",\\n  \\\"version\\\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\README.md\", \"sha256\": \"fbf52d7ea22bab1dc9e4441ed14900dac8707faee648c6291addc45d3186984e\", \"bytes\": 15576, \"text\": \"# Hosted artifact sandbox\\n\\nOne Python service provides HTTP commands and shared HTTP/MCP reads over one\\nMemgraph database. Git remains the repository's formal authority. The sandbox\\nimports a fixed snapshot and prepares drafts. The explicit Phase 3 test-copy mode\\ncan rehearse lifecycle actions on new test records. It cannot replace imported\\ndecisions or authorize real work or publication. RISK-HAG-001 remains raised:\\napplication query controls do not prove database-enforced read-only access.\\n\\nPhase 2 was verified in VREC-HAG-004. The private lifecycle pilot under WO-HAG-008\\nwas verified in [VREC-HAG-005](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification-records/VREC-HAG-005.md)\\nand integrated through PR #542. Its eight VER-HAG-006 scenarios passed.\\nThe separate native Codex/Claude qualification under WO-HAG-009 is\\n[in progress](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-009/report.md).\\nNo public service, release, authority cutover or production claim is supplied here.\\n\\n## Inputs\\n\\nUse a Linux/amd64 Docker engine with Compose and Python 3.11+ on the operator\\nhost. The service uses the immutable CPython 3.13.16 image in [Dockerfile](Dockerfile),\\nMemgraph 3.13.1 in [compose.yaml](compose.yaml), hashed [Python dependencies](requirements.lock)\\nand hashed [Git packages](system-packages.lock.json). Use only public test data.\\nKeep all outputs outside the checkout. Preserve volumes until restore comparison\\nand qualification finish. The API binds loopback; the database has no host port.\\n\\nThe governor is public evaluator 0.22.1, wheel SHA-256\\n`cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053`.\\nCandidate remote client 0.22.2 lives in another environment. Unpublished plugin\\n0.2.7 bundles the unchanged evaluator and matching remote guidance. Service\\n0.1.0.dev1 owns server dependencies; the core checker keeps zero runtime dependencies.\\n\\n## Build the exact combination\\n\\nCommit the reviewed implementation. Follow the existing\\n[release build sequence](../docs/notes/developing-se-harness.md#release-sequences)\\nto produce the 0.22.2 candidate wheel and its two-build replay JSON at that commit.\\nUse the public 0.22.1 wheel as `EVALUATOR_WHEEL`. Resolve uppercase placeholders\\nto absolute paths or selected values. Keep each path as one argument.\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py prepare --repository REPO --output PACKAGE_OUT --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --client-replay CLIENT_REPLAY_JSON --evaluator-wheel EVALUATOR_WHEEL --image LOCAL_IMAGE\\n```\\n\\nThe command refuses a dirty checkout or client replay from another commit. It\\nreads exact Git blobs, uses the existing development plugin assembler, builds\\nthe service image, and records actual component identities. Outputs are:\\n\\n- `combination.json`: built identities, marked qualification pending.\\n- `configuration/config.json`: non-secret selection for that combination.\\n- `credentials.json`: generated test principals; keep this file private.\\n- `plugin/`: separate Codex and Claude development archives and extracted trees.\\n- `candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`: the selected deployment recipe.\\n- Command results and image metadata, including failures.\\n\\nReadiness verifies the selected release, installed service bytes, runtime,\\ndatabase version/configuration, schema and complete tuple. It is not assurance.\\n\\n## Stage the historical source\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/stage.py REPO REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/reference-manifest.json SOURCE_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThis writes `source/`, `source-manifest.json` and `source-inventory.json` from\\nexact Git blobs, including original code/evidence bindings. It does not execute\\nsource files. Create a new Docker volume `SOURCE_VOLUME` and copy those three\\nentries into its root. On Windows, archive the entries and extract inside Docker\\nto avoid slow small-file reads through a Windows bind mount. Retain the archive\\ndigest and copy command. Compose mounts this source read-only.\\n\\n## Initialize and start\\n\\nSet these environment variables for every Compose command:\\n\\n| Name | Selected value |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE` | Built `LOCAL_IMAGE`; retain its inspected immutable identity |\\n| `HAG_HTTP_PORT` | An unused loopback port, for example `18080` |\\n| `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` | Populated `SOURCE_VOLUME` |\\n| `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/configuration` |\\n| `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json` |\\n\\nChoose a new Compose project `PROJECT_NAME`. `COMPOSE_FILE` is the generated\\n`candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`.\\n\\n```text\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d graph\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE run --rm service init\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d service\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE exec -T service harness-hosted ready\\n```\\n\\nWait for database availability before initialization and service readiness before\\nclient operations. Initialization is explicit; ordinary startup does not migrate\\nor repair a schema. `/health` means alive; authenticated `/v1/status` means ready.\\n\\nInstall `CLIENT_WHEEL` with `pip --no-deps` into a separate disposable environment.\\nIts Python is `CLIENT_PYTHON`. Use `-I -m se_harness remote`, never that candidate\\nas the governor. Read the extracted plugin's setup **Hosted sandbox selection**,\\nthen harness-orient or change. Native host discovery must be tested separately\\nwhere required; extracting files does not prove a host loaded the plugin.\\n\\n## Test the actual packages\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_service.py --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest SOURCE_OUT/source-manifest.json --scenario-fixture REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:PORT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThe packaged client imports and retries, retrieves the fixed work context, creates\\nand revises a draft, refuses invalid/stale writes, recovers a receipt, compares\\nviews, reads Cypher, runs the released check and freezes the draft. Each request\\nand result is retained. Its report lists remaining checks; it is not full acceptance.\\n\\nRun `tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_boundaries.py` with installed service\\ndependencies in a separate Compose service process. Mount the test directory\\nread-only and a new output directory. Pass `--walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_OUT` and\\n`--output BOUNDARY_OUT`. Default checks cover protected/malformed requests,\\nconcurrent connections, transaction faults, HTTP/MCP parity and resource limits.\\nFault hooks exist only in the test process, never on a network route.\\n\\nUse `--only lost_reply` with a separately installed candidate `--client-python`\\nand `--client-wheel` inside that process for lost-response recovery. If earlier\\nchecks advanced the context, pass their final `--continuation` JSON. Inspect the\\nretained operation before retrying any interrupted write. Never invent a new\\nexpected version or operation key to make a failed test succeed.\\n\\nRun `qualify_history.py` through the isolated released evaluator with `-I`, the\\nmounted original `--source`, `--manifest`, fixed `--fixture`, new `--output`, and\\nwalkthrough `005-work-context-result.json` as `--hosted-result`. This independent\\nprojection compares the evaluator result and recomputes legacy path/code hashes.\\n\\nFollow the complete [VER-HAG-001 matrix](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification/VER-HAG-001.md),\\nincluding import variants, missing bindings, tuple/schema failures, measured\\nlimits and native plugin observations. Skipped or absent cases are unperformed.\\nRun the applicable repository regression and distribution checks.\\n\\nRun `qualify_integrity.py` in a disposable service process with the same mounts,\\nwalkthrough and current continuation. Supply its separately installed candidate\\n`--client-python`. This checks altered deployment identities, installed service\\ncontracts, evaluator substitution, and broken context-base links. Its file edits\\naffect only the disposable container; its graph edits always roll back. Do not run\\nit inside the serving container. Passing these checks does not complete the other\\nscenario requirements.\\n\\nRun `qualify_imports.py` with the walkthrough, current continuation and a new\\noutput directory. It creates disposable copies of the original source to test\\nduplicate IDs and unresolved targets. It also rejects unsupported import formats\\nand changed bytes under the original provenance. These negative tests must not\\nchange the database.\\n\\n`qualify_time.py` measures the configured five-second database read-transaction\\nlimit. Its stress query is a direct driver test, outside the public read grammar.\\nIt must produce a resource-limit refusal. This does not by itself prove a slow\\nquery's HTTP response or replace the public Cypher admission checks.\\n\\n## Restart and restore\\n\\nKeep the same `HAG_*` environment and stop other test writers. Use a fresh output\\nand an unused restore port:\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py recover --compose COMPOSE_FILE --project PROJECT_NAME --output RECOVERY_OUT --restore-port RESTORE_PORT\\n```\\n\\nThe command fingerprints the acknowledged graph, restarts the original, stops\\nwriters/database for a consistent backup, resumes the original, and restores\\ninto a new `PROJECT_NAME-restore` volume. It refuses an existing restore volume.\\nIt compares both copies at the cutoff and records times, storage, archive digest\\nand commands. Keep the backup and both volumes. Record the archive's retained\\nlocation outside Git. This proves no power-loss, production RPO/RTO or migration claim.\\n\\n## Protocol and limits\\n\\nSee the [protocol guide](../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md) and closed\\n[command](contracts/remote-v1.json), [read](contracts/read-v1.json) and\\n[result](contracts/result-v1.json) schemas. Views are explicit. Domain and MCP\\nreads share one handler. Partial reads cannot support a governing-context claim.\\n\\nLimits: 2,500 imported artifacts; 10,000 retained revisions; 1 MiB per document;\\n64 MiB of formal import content; two evaluator slots; 500 aggregate read rows;\\n2 MiB per response; depth eight; five seconds per Cypher query; 120 seconds per\\nevaluator process. Preserve measured limitations and RISK-HAG-001. Do not expose\\nthe sandbox on a shared or untrusted network.\\n\\n## Phase 3: private lifecycle rehearsal\\n\\nThis is an opt-in test project. Supplied decision actors are synthetic labels.\\nGit remains authoritative for real definitions and decisions. Authentication and\\ndatabase ACL implementation are deferred; keep the existing private controls.\\n\\n1. Build the clean candidate client with the pinned recipe above. Prepare the\\n   service with the same command above, adding `--phase3`. The configuration selects\\n   schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`. These are local qualification packages;\\n   do not publish them or replace the user's installed plugin.\\n2. Create the small synthetic source fixture outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/prepare_lifecycle_fixture.py --evaluator-python RELEASED_PYTHON --output FIXTURE_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   `RELEASED_PYTHON` is the absolute Python path for public evaluator 0.22.1. This\\n   command uses `-I`, creates an ordinary disposable Git repository, validates the\\n   seed records and stages exact Git blobs. Copy `FIXTURE_OUT/staged/` into a new\\n   source volume with the volume procedure above.\\n3. Use a new Compose project and graph volume. Set `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE`,\\n   `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY`, `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE`, `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` and a free\\n   loopback `HAG_HTTP_PORT`. Start the stack and run its explicit `init`. Do not\\n   migrate or reuse a Phase 2 volume. Read authenticated status and require the\\n   expected package identities, schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`.\\n4. Install `CLIENT_WHEEL` into a separate environment. Run the packaged-client\\n   walkthrough, keeping its output outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_pilot.py --repository REPO --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest FIXTURE_OUT/staged/source-manifest.json --endpoint ENDPOINT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   The runner authors new test definitions, exercises a failed gate and an invalid\\n   edge, accepts definitions, starts work, records a paired risk/decision, retains\\n   handoff evidence, and prepares and assesses a test VREC and RLS. It repeats\\n   accepted requests, reads the resulting context and exports an earlier and a\\n   later baseline. Each command and actual result is retained. It does not claim\\n   the remaining fault, concurrency, recovery or independent replay checks passed.\\n5. Use the recorded v2 request files as examples for deliberate manual rehearsal.\\n   The [wire contract](contracts/lifecycle-v2.md) defines every allowed operation.\\n   Keep versions and input digest from the selected preview. After a lost reply,\\n   use the existing operation lookup before changing a key or input.\\n6. Export with an explicit new destination. The client creates `files/`,\\n   `history.bundle` and `manifest.json`. An `.incomplete` marker means the export\\n   must not be used. Clone the bundle into another new directory, compare every\\n   exported file byte-for-byte, then use released 0.22.1 there to validate and\\n   check the selected records. Keep the original test candidate P from the VREC;\\n   a later governance commit is not a replacement candidate.\\n\\nThe read-only MCP tools use the same exact selected test snapshots. Their results\\nare labeled `se-harness-graph-read/v2`; ordinary Phase 2 projects retain v1 results.\\nNo new writable MCP tool or external publication operation is present.\\n\\nPreserve test volumes until restart and restore checks finish. If Docker has no\\nautomatic subnet left, inspect its networks and host routes, then supply a Compose\\noverride with unused private subnets. Retain the override and effective Compose\\nconfiguration with the run. Keep the database private and HTTP bound to loopback;\\ndo not delete unrelated stacks to obtain address space.\\n\\nFor the required supplemental checks, run `qualify_pilot_store.py` and\\n`qualify_pilot_replay.py` from `tests/hosted_artifact_graph/` in the packaged\\nservice container. Copy the selected walkthrough output into that container;\\nuse `--state WALKTHROUGH_OUT/walkthrough.json --output STORE_RESULT.json` for\\nthe store runner and `--walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_OUT --output REPLAY_OUT` for\\nindependent replay. Both use the mounted configuration and credential files.\\nThe store runner injects faults locally; no fault-injection HTTP route exists.\\nIt tests actual transaction rollback, racing writers, retained receipts, bounds\\nand the 120-second evaluator deadline. Retain its result before continuing.\\n\\nThen run `qualify_pilot_transport.py` on the client host with the walkthrough's\\nclient, configuration, credential, source, repository and endpoint arguments.\\nSet a new `--output TRANSPORT_OUT` and `--state STORE_RESULT.json`. It drops one\\nreply after a real commit, retrieves the receipt and repeats the identical\\nrequest. Use the recovery command above afterward. With explicit subnets, add\\n`--compose-override ORIGINAL_OVERRIDE --restore-override RESTORE_OVERRIDE`;\\nthe restored stack needs separate unused ranges. Reconcile the retained operation\\nkey and re-export its baseline on both stacks. These are test decisions only.\\n\"}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

Use\\n`capture-verification` and `prepare-release` for commit-bound VREC and RLS\\ninstances; an edited template is not a substitute for their derived evidence.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8df276d2f837c4dcc663dbdb42c67cbb6f8fe3bf4abcb53acf86bc7538269a72\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"75b0c06f90fbb219fc31684a1a2d97987215dbada20e335656e45a57532c3010\", \"bytes\": 3505, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"title\": \"Links between definitions\", \"anchor\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 35, \"content\": \"## Links between definitions\\n\\nAn arrow points from the artifact that records the link to the artifact it\\nreferences. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\\n\\nRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\\ndeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\\nof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\\nPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\\nThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\\nvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CAP[\\\"Capability (CAP)\\\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\\\"Intent (INT)\\\"]\\n    REQ[\\\"Requirement (REQ)\\\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\\n    SPEC[\\\"Specification (SPEC)\\\"] -->|specifies| REQ\\n    VER[\\\"Verification contract (VER)\\\"] -->|verifies| REQ\\n    ARCH[\\\"Architecture (ARCH)\\\"] -->|addresses| REQ\\n    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\\n    ADR[\\\"Architecture decision (ADR)\\\"] -->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\\n| Requirement (REQ) \\u2192 Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\\n| Specification (SPEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Verification contract (VER) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7e7361437700c3a1bf7d9add02accf3a4d3ee3fa48dbdc0ba0b991b40514071a\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}, {\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}, {\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"c4ffde0efff3a57df41cf6b282896e6827ea289607f8b73faa8f7c09d0c70213\", \"bytes\": 8654, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nDefinitions, work scope and verification requirements are ready for work planning.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3977586afdaba8e900cfd38bfd72b02ccf3d011048dae4b247fe81a24c64c9cc\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo), [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope) and [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d2a9a7707114a465ebde20884e2a996807663ab4aa94ff11008f2360617efe50\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"title\": \"Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 143, \"content\": \"### Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, artifact inventory, definition drafts,\\namendment proposals, verification contracts (VER), risks (RISK), and\\nunresolved decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or completed work orders (WO) in `draft`.\\n  Applicable risks (RISK) and open decisions (DEC) updated with the actual\\n  work order (WO) links. Lifecycle states and dispositions are preserved.\\n  Approved work orders (WO) remain unchanged; proposed scope changes require\\n  review.\\n- **Transient working material:** The review handoff and evaluator results.\\n  Retain these under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the implementation and follow its callers, references and consumers.\\n   Check tests and fixtures, instructions and documentation, packaging and CI,\\n   and verification outputs where they apply. Keep the working inventory in\\n   the conversation or temporary storage outside the repository.\\n   Group each complete, independently verifiable outcome into one bounded\\n   work order with its necessary supporting changes.\\n2. Select an existing work order (WO) in `draft` for a unit only if its scope\\n   matches. Otherwise, create a new work order (WO) with the commands below.\\n3. Complete each draft using the field table below. In Expected change\\n   surface, name the inspected paths and give a short reason for each.\\n   Explain non-applicable areas and unknown destinations briefly.\\n4. Check that every selected requirement (REQ) has the specification (SPEC)\\n   and verification contract (VER) coverage defined in [Complete work scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope).\\n5. Apply `## work_order` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n6. Add the new work order (WO) IDs to applicable `threatens` relations in risks\\n   (RISK) and `concerns` or `blocks` relations in open decisions (DEC). Keep\\n   every blocked ID in `concerns`. Preserve any required pairing between the\\n   risk (RISK) and decision (DEC).\\n7. If the planned change needs a missing release or operating contract,\\n   use [Prepare a release or operating contract](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract) now that the work\\n   order IDs exist. Include its draft in the proposed package.\\n8. Run the validation command below.\\n9. Correct findings within the proposed drafts. Rerun validation after edits.\\n   Report unrelated findings separately. Retain findings that need a decision\\n   or an accepted-definition amendment as unresolved dependencies.\\n10. Run the selected-work check below for each proposed work order (WO).\\n    Supply every planned file from Expected change surface with\\n    `--planned-path`. Inspect `scope.preparation`: resolve uncovered or\\n    invalid paths in the draft before requesting approval. A successful\\n    command exit does not establish coverage or a complete impact analysis.\\n    Explain future generated destinations using\\n    [Generated outputs](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs).\\n11. Present the outcome, scope, artifact IDs and paths, validation results,\\n    unresolved decisions (DEC), and unapplied amendments. Include the\\n    evaluator's reported next action for each selected work order (WO).\\n\\n| Field or section | Content |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `Objective` | The outcome this work order (WO) will deliver. |\\n| `In scope` / `Out of scope` | The boundaries from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) assigned to this work order (WO). |\\n| `Constraints` | The conditions from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) that apply to this work. |\\n| `Expected change surface` | Inspected planned paths, the reason for each, and unresolved destinations. |\\n| `[execution_scope].paths` | Exact repository-relative files or component directories ending in `/`. Use forward slashes; no wildcards, absolute paths, or `..`. |\\n| `Authorized decision envelope` | What the implementer may decide and what requires another accountable decision. |\\n| `Required verification` / `Evidence to record` | The checks and retained outputs defined in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified). |\\n| `Stop and escalate conditions` | The conditions that require pausing this work. |\\n| `Completion report format` | The required report of completed behavior, checks, limitations, and next accountable decision. |\\n| `[assurance]` | `commit_bound_verification`, its `rationale`, and `decided_by`. Apply the classification rules in [Assurance classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Record the human who confirmed the classification; an agent may propose it and record that human's decision. |\\n| `[relations]` | `implements` \\u2192 requirements (REQ); `specifications` \\u2192 specifications (SPEC); `verification` \\u2192 verification contracts (VER); `architecture` \\u2192 applicable architectures (ARCH) and required architecture decisions (ADR). |\\n\\nFor PR-based work, include the proposed [review-publication grant](AUTHORITY.md#review-publication-authority)\\nin the decision envelope. Name its repository, source branch, target branch\\nand selected work. Include both the ready-record publication and the later\\ndecision-only push in the expected scope. Present that grant explicitly with\\nimplementation approval; do not infer it from ordinary work authority.\\n\\nIf the assurance classification has not been confirmed, present it as a\\nproposal in the review handoff. Report the missing decision. Do not fill\\n`decided_by` with the draft author's name or an example identity to satisfy\\nvalidation. The human may confirm the classification while reviewing the\\nwork order; record that decision before previewing approval.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new work order (WO), run the creation sequence from [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions).\\nInspect the preview before creation; replace `WO-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --id WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nValidate the formal artifacts after completing the drafts and links:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nInspect each proposed work order (WO) using its actual ID:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nTo assess the proposed file list, repeat `--planned-path` for every file:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --planned-path PATH --planned-path ANOTHER-PATH --json\\n```\\n\\nThis option is available only when the selected released evaluator supports\\nit. If it is unavailable, report that version gap; do not run candidate\\nsource to govern the repository.\\n\\nThe optional planning view evaluates no checkpoint. It reports explicit\\nscope matches, existing automatic admission, uncovered paths and invalid\\ndeclarations. It does not inspect dependencies for the agent, prove that\\nthe supplied list is complete, or turn planned paths into observed changes.\\nDo not combine it with checkpoint or actual-change inputs.\\n\\nValidation does not approve the change. The checkpoint-free `check` reports\\nlifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint gates.\\n\\n**Completion:** Draft work orders (WO) are presented for review with their\\ngoverning artifacts and evaluator results. Every unresolved dependency is\\nidentified. Preparation does not approve or start execution.\\n\\n**Later use:** The authorization process reviews this artifact package,\\nresolves approval blockers, and applies permitted lifecycle transitions.\\nOnly the formal artifacts carry lasting definitions and work authority;\\ntransient working material is not persisted in the repository.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee93a263dcebc650ee59519ecaafa4c005120db60b83b8acc6bf4191efe3c8dd\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"title\": \"Links from work orders (WO)\", \"anchor\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 28, \"content\": \"## Links from work orders (WO)\\n\\nA work order (WO) selects the definitions and verification contracts (VER) that govern\\nits execution. Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\\nrelease.\\n\\nA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\\n`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\\nverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\\nor the links to verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ad947ba93cfc84640c82a0b165448ce2c15f04beed36f65a3dc031e4287aab3\"}, {\"heading\": \"generated-outputs\", \"title\": \"Generated outputs\", \"anchor\": \"generated-outputs\", \"start_line\": 66, \"end_line\": 85, \"content\": \"## Generated outputs\\n\\nExisting scope rules admit the selected work order's own file, records that\\ndirectly verify or release that work order, and those records' declared\\nevaluator-evidence paths. This does not admit those records' parent directories.\\nThe selected work order's own packet directory is also already admitted by\\nthe existing scope rules; the planning report identifies that separate rule.\\n\\nList other planned evidence, review and log destinations explicitly in the\\nwork order's scope unless an existing rule covers them. A neighboring file\\nor a record linked only to another work order is not automatically admitted.\\nThe conditional rule for recording risks during execution remains unchanged;\\nit is not a blanket admission of future files during preparation.\\n\\nIf a future record's ID is not allocated, mark its destination as unresolved\\nand explain the relationship rule expected to cover it. Do not create a\\nrecord or invent an ID to complete the plan. Once the evaluator prepares\\nthe record, assess its actual returned record and evidence paths. An\\nunresolved destination is not an already covered file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"21cb2760e5cf61158c5d19cca2af8dbe727ecf3df32247987cc1636059bde3e9\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,

}

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA risk or unresolved formal question affects the selected change.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2c0226a6752c15139cda1b7192d98f116d9947c483e5c62826c624c81a55c11a\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore writing, read [Links for decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks), [Blocking decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions) and [Raised risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"title\": \"Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\", \"anchor\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"### Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, selected definitions, verification coverage,\\nand existing risks (RISK) found in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New risks (RISK) in `raised` for threats not already\\n  covered. A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`. When that decision exists, it names the risk in `concerns`, and\\nits `blocks` set MUST equal the risk's `threatens` set. Disposing the paired\\ndecision applies its recorded effect to the risk in the same operation.\\nThe blocked artifacts change state only through their own transitions.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"dcbef84857f6b71fbfa2099de79f6caa4d82e8977b13465eccb762ffc3a9ea1e\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8b18d925f39f314acc9ea6bcc9820015c4c9430d836144e85bc31b670752371b\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"title\": \"Assess the proposed artifact package\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"start_line\": 32, \"end_line\": 83, \"content\": \"### Assess the proposed artifact package\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected work order (WO) IDs, proposed definitions, validation\\nresults, and existing decision records (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A review list identifying the selected\\n  artifacts, their states, applicable checks, and reported blockers.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run validation for the repository.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with the command below.\\n3. Read the work order (WO) and its returned reading manifest.\\n4. Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Keep unrelated findings\\n   separate.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint transition --target approved --json\\n```\\n\\nRead the result of each required check. A `pass` satisfies that check only;\\nit does not approve the artifacts or authorize implementation. If a required\\ncheck returns `fail` or `not_assessable`, report its identifier and stated\\nreason, then follow \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d Do not proceed with the\\naffected approval.\\n\\nThe last command evaluates work-order approval gates. A checkpoint-free\\n`check` only reports lifecycle context. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. Do not remove an unresolved\\nquestion merely to make validation pass.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected package has an explicit list of review findings\\nand approval blockers. No approval is inferred from these checks.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) resolves the blockers. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) presents the package for a\\nhuman decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2ea6b051236e13dd427317722d16ce7941ef5a4eb4789f7fdf568ab3d0cae3c0\"}, {\"heading\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"title\": \"Apply the selected transitions\", \"anchor\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"start_line\": 221, \"end_line\": 270, \"content\": \"### Apply the selected transitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact artifact IDs, target states, accountable human identities,\\nreviewed file digests, decisions from [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision), and clarification answers from\\n[Define the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#procedure) that must be retained in the transition reason.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only explicitly selected definitions and work orders\\n  (WO) receive the applied state and lifecycle-history entries.\\n- **Transient working material:** The preview and apply results, including\\n  any refused transition.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the reviewed artifact contents still match the human decision.\\n2. Select only the named transitions. Approve governing definitions before\\n   dependent work, or use one explicitly selected packet for mutually\\n   dependent definitions when the evaluator permits it.\\n3. Preview the transition command below.\\n4. Compare every selected ID, target state, actor, and reported effect with\\n   the human decision. Resolve failed gates before proceeding.\\n5. Recheck reviewed definition digests immediately before applying.\\n6. Repeat the passing command with `--apply`. Do not add related artifacts\\n   that the human did not select.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each clarification below the formal-decision threshold, add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Question and confirmed answer\\\"` to both the preview\\nand apply command. Use the actual question and answer. When one artifact\\nhas several such answers, combine them into one reason value for that ID.\\nKeep each complete `ID=TEXT` value as one argument. Confirm the saved reason\\nin the resulting lifecycle entry before discarding the working notes.\\n\\nFor approval, `TARGET` is `approved`. For rejection, use `rejected` and add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both commands. Rejection is\\nterminal. For a packet, repeat `--set` and `--decision` for every explicitly\\nselected artifact. Preview and apply must contain the same assignments.\\n\\n**Completion:** The evaluator reports the actual applied transitions, or the\\nspecific refusal. A successful preview alone changes nothing.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Confirm the authorization result](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#confirm-the-authorization-result) confirms the resulting authority and readiness.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c5215dec9f35d1a99bf6e4d658a594a31dc544131e70db49b1b8f79514e124b8\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"decision-rights\", \"title\": \"Decision rights\", \"anchor\": \"decision-rights\", \"start_line\": 19, \"end_line\": 80, \"content\": \"## Decision rights\\n\\nA profile describes who performs an action. A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. The selected IDs, reviewed content, target states,\\nand reason MUST still match the decision at apply time.\\n\\nThe following stable IDs name rights and operations, not additional profiles.\\nAll applicable gates remain required.\\n\\nThese DR-* identifiers come from the selected evaluator's decision-right\\ncatalogue. Use the right and exact action returned by that evaluator. Legacy\\nowner labels identify recorded accountabilities; they do not create additional\\nHuman/Agent profiles or assign a decision to a person by themselves.\\n\\n| Right ID                   | Accountable profile and authority                                                                                                  | Required input                                                                                                    | Result                                                                                               |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `DR-DEFINITION-DECIDE`     | Human authorized to decide the selected definition.                                                                                | Complete definition, exact proposed state, and required checks.                                                   | Decision on that definition only.                                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-SELECT`             | Human authorized to approve the work scope.                                                                                        | Complete governing chain, bounded work order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Completed scope, passing handoff checks, and retained evidence.                                                   | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may carry out the preparation.                                               | Exact release contract, candidate, included work, verification coverage, version, and passing preparation checks. | One `ready` release record; no release decision.                                                     |\\n| `DR-RLS-DECIDE`            | Human authorized to make the release decision.                                                                                     | Ready release record, assessed contract obligations, and the exact release or reject decision.                    | Decision on that release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. With the option absent, ACTOR must itself\\nmatch an eligible owner. The command does not authenticate either claim or\\ngrant consent. Do not infer a binding from the decision's own owners, an\\nearlier approval, Git configuration or the agent's identity.\\n\\nSilence, elapsed time, a commit, a pull request, tool execution, or a passing\\ncheck MUST NOT count as a human decision. A rejection MUST include a non-empty\\nreason. Supersession MUST name exactly one eligible successor. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ecaeb29429bcaa4eac99857f2f921e270c4865d1edeec96f536d09eb6c3130a\"}, {\"heading\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"title\": \"Delegation and separation\", \"anchor\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"start_line\": 111, \"end_line\": 133, \"content\": \"## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f07389fbbe529ad544d8b7d7f18894bfa45f0ec69996c93ed8372416b55ddf91\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RESULTS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"090e0172a78ebedfe4cdbe98e74c171e50215766a4ebbd671844a89af3f72e6e\", \"bytes\": 5242, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nReport a governed result, handle a refusal or recover an uncertain operation.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"680ff724251b96e21b52d9104a0e6f2806e6f4269237b555518e7d72d20463a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead only the actual selected result and evidence needed to establish its effects. Before eligible English reporting, read [COMMUNICATION.md#communication](COMMUNICATION.md#communication) if it is no longer in context.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"22e8f880f3e2c5192c3f6abf5f63c7542b51647503ba0fb877c5acb70c7a5837\"}, {\"heading\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"title\": \"Report a lifecycle result\", \"anchor\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 46, \"content\": \"### Report a lifecycle result\\n\\nAfter a lifecycle stage completes or reaches a stop condition, obtain the\\nselected evaluator's schema-2 result. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. The actual artifact IDs and whether the selected operation completed or\\n   was blocked.\\n2. The observed effects, separately from expected effects that did not occur.\\n3. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. In particular, do not\\n   imply approval, a transition, verification, release, a Git action,\\n   publication, deployment, or operation that did not occur.\\n4. The final lifecycle state and the accountable human or agent. When a\\n   decision is required, name the exact decision and authority needed.\\n5. Exactly one current typed procedure step from the evaluator.\\n6. The command's argument values and boundaries, or the operative meaning of\\n   the suggested response.\\n\\nOnly complete alternatives declared by the workflow may be shown. Present them\\nseparately from the primary next step. Do not invent an effect, authority,\\nblocker, decision, or alternative. Do not add unrelated repository findings\\nto the selected result. Do not replace the returned next step with an\\nopen-ended question about what to do next.\\n\\nAutomation MUST read the structured JSON result. New results declare\\n`digest_format = \\\"machine-fields-v1\\\"`. This digest binds machine fields such\\nas candidate identity, scope, state, gates, and command arguments. Explanatory\\nwording is excluded. Older retained results keep their original digest format.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d12f5fc7e6190762622666754fde9b70e658249ceb41f2fdbf48e5e0edbd0f8f\"}]}]}\r\n",
