  "command": "\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\.cache\\\\codex-runtimes\\\\codex-primary-runtime\\\\dependencies\\\\native\\\\powershell\\\\pwsh.exe\" -Command '& \"C:/Users/mathi/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe\" -I \"C:/Users/mathi/Documents/Codex/2026-09-20/verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se/work/h43/f/codex-401/native/inputs/native_call.py\" instructions --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions\" --section \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk\" --section \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision\"'",
  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA risk or unresolved formal question affects the selected change.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2c0226a6752c15139cda1b7192d98f116d9947c483e5c62826c624c81a55c11a\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore writing, read [Links for decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks), [Blocking decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions) and [Raised risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"risk\", \"title\": \"risk\", \"anchor\": \"risk\", \"start_line\": 188, \"end_line\": 198, \"content\": \"## risk\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\\n- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\\n- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1\\u20135); the command computes their product.\\n- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\\n- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\\n\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8815c9ff38ca34594404ab95cb0545053e209804030f3d635a50641d33559de9\"}, {\"heading\": \"decision\", \"title\": \"decision\", \"anchor\": \"decision\", \"start_line\": 171, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## decision\\n\\nA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\\nof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\\napproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\\nand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\\n- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\\n- A deviation also names `against = \\\"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\\\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\\n- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\\n- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\\n- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\\n- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "command": "\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\.cache\\\\codex-runtimes\\\\codex-primary-runtime\\\\dependencies\\\\native\\\\powershell\\\\pwsh.exe\" -Command \"& \\\"C:/Users/mathi/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe\\\" -I \\\"C:/Users/mathi/Documents/Codex/2026-09-20/verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se/work/h43/f/codex-401/native/inputs/native_call.py\\\" read-text \\\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\contracts\\\\lifecycle-v2.md\\\"\"",
  "aggregated_output": "{\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\contracts\\\\lifecycle-v2.md\", \"sha256\": \"9f1c02ef540c00fa739beb6521295ba9b068f3ab66ff0b0b196cb95810dcd601\", \"bytes\": 5989, \"text\": \"# Private lifecycle rehearsal wire contract\\n\\nThe v2 endpoint accepts only `lifecycle-v2.json`. Every request and result selects\\ntest data. Git remains authoritative for real work. Existing v1 routes and the\\nseven read-only MCP tools keep their contract; they cannot dispatch v2 actions.\\nIn an explicitly configured test project their results use\\n`se-harness-graph-read/v2`, with a required test-copy label. Ordinary Phase 2\\nprojects retain their v1 read result shapes. Revision byte hashing is unchanged;\\ntest revisions add explicit test-copy provenance, without rewriting v1 fixtures.\\n\\n`inspect` accepts check, preflight and validate. `preview` runs a mutation in a\\ndiscarded projection and returns its input digest and complete proposed file\\neffects. `apply` requires that digest, reruns the released checks, and commits\\nthe complete result once. A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\n\\nRelationship paths are supported. Use `-[edge:TYPE]->` or `<-[edge:TYPE]-` between\\nlabelled nodes, with a public relationship type from the physical representation.\\nEach node and relationship needs a distinct variable name. Anonymous relationship\\nsyntax such as `-[:TYPE]->` is refused; a refusal of that form does not mean\\nrelationship traversal is unsupported. Return-column aliases (`AS alias`) are\\noptional.\\n\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}\r\n",

Keep approval, start,\\nverification and release as separate observations when their requests are separate.\\nDistinguish `previewed`, `accepted` and `refused`. Cite each retained request/result; do not\\ncombine their outcomes. Keep the import baseline distinct from later exports.\\n\\nState observed behavior separately from supported behavior. A refused query\\nestablishes the refusal of that query. Read the public query contract before\\nclaiming that a label, property or relationship is unsupported, or that a clause\\nis required. Link the source for a general capability claim; otherwise omit it.\\n\\nInclude material failures, recovered errors, permission denials and uncertain\\neffects. Identify whether the host, client or service refused the action. Use a\\ncaptured call summary for counts when available; do not estimate from memory.\\nState what each count measures. Tool-error counts can exclude service refusals\\nreturned inside normal tool responses; report those refusals separately.\\nIf the capture is incomplete, say which result or count remains unassessed.\\n\\nName identities in full: hosted input baseline B, source fixture commit S,\\ntest Git candidate P, and actual implementation candidate C. The selected test\\ninputs name C in `qualification_candidate`; the bounded helper's `identity` result\\nalso returns that value. Inspect and cite this input before calling C unknown.\\nIf an identity is not established by the cited evidence, report it as unknown.   "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8b18d925f39f314acc9ea6bcc9820015c4c9430d836144e85bc31b670752371b\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"title\": \"Resolve approval blockers\", \"anchor\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"start_line\": 84, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead7ade46e1090c644d789a5ca1155415aa2497561938b885e8316cd13aeb920\"}]}]}\r\n",

For a scope finding, read [RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked](RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5581ca4e192b2a3847952cdb19582916ed96242a14941b1e5a8a610be996e1dd\"}, {\"heading\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"title\": \"Start the selected work\", \"anchor\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 104, \"content\": \"### Start the selected work\\n\\n**Inputs:** The approved work order (WO), actual executor identity, and\\ncurrent execution context.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `in_progress`\\n  with a lifecycle-history entry when start succeeds.\\n- **Transient working material:** Start-check and transition results.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If the work order (WO) is already `in_progress`, inspect the recorded start\\n   and resume unapplied work. Do not replay the start transition.\\n2. Otherwise, run start preflight under the existing approval.\\n3. Preview the transition to `in_progress` using the actual executor identity.\\n4. Apply the same transition only when preflight and the preview pass.\\n5. Inspect the resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected work order (WO) is `in_progress`, or its start\\nis blocked with an explicit reason. Existing approval covers a permitted\\nstart; no duplicate human start decision is required.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Implement the approved scope](EXECUTE_WORK.md#implement-the-approved-scope) performs the authorized implementation.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2275126fa8b418eccbaacb1972d0140709337470ba8d190b6566fd16854328d1\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"title\": \"Authority from work approval\", \"anchor\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"start_line\": 134, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## Authority from work approval\\n\\nWork-order approval authorizes execution of its approved scope: start,\\nimplementation, local edits and commits, required checks, evidence capture,\\ncompletion recording, and required verification-record preparation. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. An older approval without\\nsuch a grant needs an authorized amendment for the remaining execution.\\nCurrent metadata or an actor label MUST NOT manufacture that historical grant.\\nIf the installed release cannot record the required authorization, stop the\\nremaining execution and report the missing historical grant and the lack of\\na supported amendment operation. Do not insert invented grant fields or\\nrewrite the old approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"a0ce00fccb8c1c8833455c14fe3ec75eaf01c597f0a1f46a24f7962ab1958f8c\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"f094e7bc796ba1002c3fb2848adaccce6c4887e3d92503911bcafa4504a644fe\", \"bytes\": 11979, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects work start, implementation or completion under matching authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b7fc3711b437c73d3cc5cce46c0a8bb7f1bc3c8c98ba650b4b046950d69a7652\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead the selected work order and governing artifacts returned by the evaluator. Before using its execution grant, read [AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval](AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval). For a scope finding, read [RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked](RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5581ca4e192b2a3847952cdb19582916ed96242a14941b1e5a8a610be996e1dd\"}, {\"heading\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"title\": \"Retain the implementation evidence\", \"anchor\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"start_line\": 155, \"end_line\": 210, \"content\": \"### Retain the implementation evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The implemented changes, verification contracts (VER), required\\nrepository checks, and work-order evidence locations.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** Actual check results, review findings, their\\n  resolution, and Git-derived handoff evidence at authorized evidence paths.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Evidence references may be added where the work order\\n  (WO) requires them. No lifecycle state changes here.\\n- **Transient working material:** A summary of remaining evidence gaps.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run every required check using its specified inputs and environment.\\n2. Retain the command arguments, working directory, runtime identity, exit\\n   status, output, and relevant file paths or digests.\\n3. Preserve failed results alongside later corrections and successful reruns.\\n4. Retain the material diff-review findings and their resolution.\\n5. Confirm that all required evidence files exist at the locations named by\\n   the work order (WO) or verification contract (VER).\\n6. Run review preflight.\\n7. Run the Git-derived handoff check with the trusted `BASE` from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n8. Inspect its written evidence and reported findings. Correct in-scope gaps\\n   and rerun affected checks.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase review --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nFor ordinary files listed in the work order\\u2019s `evidence_paths`, confirm that\\neach file exists inside the repository and contains the required evidence.\\nThese files do not need a machine header. Use the supported evidence command\\nfor generated packets; do not edit their evaluator-owned binding fields.\\n\\nThe Git-derived handoff command writes retained evidence. Confirm its output\\npaths are covered by the approved preparation scope. If the evaluator calls\\nfor creating or rebinding the handoff evidence packet, use:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl evidence REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --json\\n```\\n\\nThis command also writes a file. It does not run tests or make an unsupported\\nclaim true. Rerun the required handoff check after correcting the evidence gap.\\n\\n**Completion:** Required implementation checks pass and the actual evidence\\nis retained, or the exact missing or failed checks remain visible.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record implementation completion](EXECUTE_WORK.md#record-implementation-completion) requires passing handoff results. Verification later\\nassesses these retained files; they are not disposable planning notes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"4cccfe03ac5fe219da997051bb91053576f18e67e834f0036f93e9856e8f12a2\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"title\": \"Record implementation completion\", \"anchor\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"start_line\": 211, \"end_line\": 257, \"content\": \"### Record implementation completion\\n\\n**Inputs:** Completed work, passing handoff checks, retained evidence, and\\nthe unchanged approved execution scope.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `implemented`\\n  with the actual executor recorded in its lifecycle history.\\n- **Transient working material:** The completion report and current next step.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the work and required evidence are complete.\\n2. Preview the completion transition using the executor's own identity.\\n3. Apply the same transition when the preview passes.\\n4. Inspect the resulting work order (WO).\\n5. Report the completed behavior, checks, limitations, and evaluator's next\\n   action. Preserve failures if completion was refused.\\n\\nUse the passing handoff result from the preceding step. A passing completion\\npreview does not replace the handoff check. If the implementation, governing\\nartifacts, or required evidence changed after handoff, rerun the affected\\nchecks before applying completion. If `harnessctl` refuses the retained\\nhandoff evidence, follow its reported corrective step.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The work order (WO) is `implemented`, or its completion is\\nblocked. Completion does not verify, release, or deliver the result.\\n\\n**Later use:** Work requiring commit-bound verification proceeds to\\n[Verify the outcome](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#establish-the-verification-scope).\\nAfter preparation, PR-based work first follows [Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package).\\nThen use the [verification request](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision)\\nwhen the ready record is eligible and its PR is confirmed. Local-only work\\nuses that verification request without a PR. The completion report introduces no\\nadditional human approval. An implemented work order (WO) classified `not_required`\\nneeds no new verification record (VREC); follow its actual next action and\\nany separately authorized delivery instruction.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e9c897ed3281727176649c1a128308da088e0f04282645d2c43a4c7a9a795649\"}, {\"heading\": \"implement-the-approved-scope\", \"title\": \"Implement the approved scope\", \"anchor\": \"implement-the-approved-scope\", \"start_line\": 105, \"end_line\": 154, \"content\": \"### Implement the approved scope\\n\\n**Inputs:** The work order (WO) in `in_progress`, approved definitions,\\npermitted paths, and baseline from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Repository files:** The code, tests, documentation, or configuration\\n  changes authorized by the work order (WO).\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No lifecycle transition in this step. Artifact content\\n  changes require the authority and procedure applicable to those records.\\n- **Transient working material:** Implementation notes and unresolved findings.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the files and behavior to be changed.\\n2. Compare the complete actual and planned path set with the approved scope.\\n3. Run the scope check below with every actual and planned path.\\n4. Make the changes allowed by the work order (WO).\\n5. Run local checks as needed to guide the implementation. Keep failures\\n   available for the evidence record.\\n6. Review the diff against the accepted definitions. Apply\\n   [Review of implemented changes](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#review-of-implemented-changes).\\n7. Resolve in-scope defects. Stop affected work when a finding requires changed\\n   requirements, paths, or authority.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nRepeat `--changed-path PATH` for the complete set, including planned new files:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint scope --changed-path PATH --changes-complete --json\\n```\\n\\nThis declaration is checked evidence, not independent proof of completeness.\\nWhen the selected procedure requires a `pre-action` check, use its returned\\ncommand with the complete change-set inputs. For Git-derived actual changes:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint pre-action --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the repository's editing, build, and test tools for implementation.\\n`harnessctl` does not implement the change.\\n\\n**Completion:** The approved behavior is implemented within scope, or the\\nremaining work and blocker are explicit. No completion state is inferred yet.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Retain the implementation evidence](EXECUTE_WORK.md#retain-the-implementation-evidence) checks the result and retains its evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"fccc0b61295d1a2fb0b7f7a3323063932bed26eafce5d7f592a432d9493ec944\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "status": "completed"
}

Preserve the observed evidence.\\nUse the evaluator's current result to report one corrective step or one\\naccountable escalation.\\n\\nFor a failed gate, use the corrective form that `harnessctl check` returns for\\nthe first failing predicate. Reuse it only if its\\napproved scope covers the correction and its current state permits execution.\\nStart approved work through the start procedure; resume work already in\\nprogress. If no eligible work order covers the correction, return to Define\\nthe change and Authorize the work to prepare and approve a new work order.\\nPreserve completed and rejected records. A correction that changes an accepted\\ndefinition must also follow the linked-revision boundary.\\n\\nAfter an interrupted write or uncertain external action, inspect the actual\\nresult before retrying. The score describes the knowledge expected from the reader, not the quality or complexity of the document. -->\\n\\n> This is a non-authoritative reference to command syntax, actors and side\\n> effects. The selected released evaluator computes lifecycle states, allowed\\n> transitions, gates and next actions. Start with\\n> [ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, heading `read-by-task`), then use\\n> [CONTINUE.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md`, heading `continue-selected-work`),\\n> [decision rights](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md`, heading `decision-rights`) and\\n> [results](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md`, heading `report-a-lifecycle-result`) when directed.\\n\\n## Invocation\\n\\nIn evaluator examples, `harnessctl` means the absolute Python executable of\\nthe repository's selected released evaluator followed by `-I -m se_harness`.\\nRun it from outside the checkout. `REPO` is the absolute repository path;\\nreplace placeholders before running a command. Source-development commands\\nare identified separately and do not govern repository lifecycle state.\\n\\nFor example, with `CHECKER` replaced by that absolute executable:\\n\\n```text\\n\\\"CHECKER\\\" -I -m se_harness check \\\"REPO\\\" --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nIn PowerShell, prefix a quoted executable with `&`. Run\\n`harnessctl COMMAND --help` for the exact parser help in the selected environment.\\nThe syntax inventory below shows parser defaults and optional inputs; always\\nsupply an absolute `TARGET` for repository operations from the external directory.\\n\\n## Command shape\\n\\nThese rules describe the local evaluator commands (`WO-ECP-022`).\\nThe unpublished hosted `remote` client has the separate contract below:\\n\\n- **The repository is the positional `TARGET`**, default `.`, on every\\n  command that reads or writes one. `select-work-order` reads an event file,\\n  `identity` reads a runtime environment and `qualify candidate-package`\\n  reads a wheel, so they take none. `skill-ownership` requires an explicit\\n  positional `TARGET` under SPEC-PLG-020; it has no implicit repository selection.\\n- **Naming.** `--artifact` selects an existing artifact; `--id` names the\\n  record a command creates; an option that names a relation of that record\\n  keeps the relation's name (`--work-order`, `--verification`,\\n  `--verification-record`, `--release-contract`). Both record commands name\\n  their preparation actor `--owner`. `preflight` keeps `--work-order`\\n  until it folds into `check`.\\n- **`--json` everywhere.** The workflow commands print the schema-2 result;\\n  `validate`, `validate-draft`, `inspect`, `resources`, `release-unit`, `identity`\\n  and `qualify` print their own objects; every other command prints one\\n  `se-harness-command-result-v1` object with the same facts as its human\\n  output.\\n- **Plan and write.** A command that changes existing governed state\\n  (`transition`, `decide`, `upgrade`, `skill-ownership`) plans by\\n  default and writes only with `--apply`. A command that adds content\\n  (`init`, `scaffold-domain`, `create-artifact`) writes by default and\\n  plans with `--dry-run`; `init` into a target with content appends the\\n  bounded fragments to existing files and refuses every other difference.\\n- **Exit codes.** `0`: completed. `1`: the command ran and its result is\\n  failed, blocked or not passing. `2`: the command could not run (a usage\\n  error, a refusal before any result). A failed result goes to standard\\n  output in both renderings; a code appears once per line.\\n\\n## Command inventory\\n\\n| Command | Principal actor | State effect | Intended use |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `remote` | authorized sandbox operator or author; reader for reads | explicit remote reads or bounded sandbox draft writes; no local fallback | use the separate\", \"offset\": 0, \"next_offset\": 4096, \"complete\": false, \"characters\": 64034}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"84686ea50e0e220aadc024145b88e05d83a0eab01be361ab50e12716a8cf950a\", \"bytes\": 18538, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects verification preparation, review or a verification decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f126342ca298b7ef6382ce9da4dd1934b190bcac8937c142c015fe5f43092015\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor preparation, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage). For a decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). For supersession only, also read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage). Read the exact candidate and retained evidence required by the selected contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"509b10e8e12887c623b12e5997e2baf7bcb193b87a24b63fe19795676bddc8a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare the verification record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"start_line\": 108, \"end_line\": 169, \"content\": \"### Prepare the verification record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact candidate, selected work orders (WO), their verification\\ncontracts (VER), retained evidence, and existing preparation authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** One new verification record (VREC) in `ready` when\\n  capture is required and succeeds. Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"title\": \"Assess the verification evidence\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"### Assess the verification evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected candidate, accepted definitions, verification\\ncontracts (VER), and retained implementation evidence.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** A requirement-by-requirement assessment with\\n  actual check results and unresolved gaps at the specified evidence locations.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No verification decision or lifecycle transition.\\n- **Transient working material:** Review notes not required as retained evidence.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

For a decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). For supersession only, also read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage). Read the exact candidate and retained evidence required by the selected contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"509b10e8e12887c623b12e5997e2baf7bcb193b87a24b63fe19795676bddc8a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Historical candidate and evidence facts are preserved.\\n- **Transient working material:** The observed decision result and next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Recheck that the selected inputs still match the human decision.\\n2. Preview the exact transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Preserve\\nthe old record; do not rewrite its candidate or evidence to match a new result.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected verification record (VREC) has the recorded\\ndecision. Referenced work orders (WO) and release records (RLS) remain unchanged.\\n\\n**Later use:** For PR-based work, [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision)\\nas the final commit under the existing grant. Eligible verified coverage\\nsupports the selected delivery path.\\nA rejection or supersession follows the evaluator's remediation or selection\\nprocedure; it does not authorize new implementation scope.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"99e090908551d2012bdadac654496a2c14eefe9399b04112fcf067f6386854d7\"}, {\"heading\": \"obtain-the-humans-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Obtain the human's verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"obtain-the-humans-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 170, \"end_line\": 254, \"content\": \"### Obtain the human's verification decision\\n\\nFor work delivered through a PR, first complete\\n[Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package).\\nDo not request verification before the exact remote review package is confirmed.\\nUse the evaluator's declared review-publication alternative, not its later\\nintegration path. Local-only work does not acquire a PR requirement.\\n\\n**Inputs:** The ready verification record (VREC), candidate commit, evidence\\ndigests, assessment results, and accountable human's verification authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by the discussion or read-only gate check.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's exact verification, rejection,\\n  or supersession decision and reason where required.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Prepare the concise verification request below for the exact record,\\n   candidate, evidence, and unresolved findings.\\n2. For verification or rejection, evaluate the proposed target with the\\n   command below. Supersession gates are evaluated with the selected successor\\n   in [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision)'s transition preview.\\n3. Obtain the accountable human's decision on that exact verification record\\n   (VREC). Preserve the required independence from implementation.\\n4. Reuse a previous decision only while its record, candidate, evidence digests,\\n   authority, and current gates still match.\\n5. For rejection, retain the reason. For supersession, identify the exact\\n   eligible successor verification record (VREC).\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `verified` or `rejected` for `TARGET`. The evaluator determines whether\\nthat edge is legal. Supersession needs the successor input accepted by\\n`transition --reason`, which this check command does not accept.\\nA passed check is not the human decision.\\n\\n**Verification request:**\\n\\n- **Verification requested - [outcome]:** Name the useful result being assessed.\\n- **Delivered:** Describe the behavior delivered against the agreed outcome.\\n- **Evidence:** Summarize the requirement results and meaningful checks. Link\\n  the requirement-by-requirement assessment and retained evidence. Test counts\\n  support the explanation; they do not replace it.\\n- **Limits:** State material failures, skipped or unavailable checks, unassessed\\n  criteria, and residual uncertainty. Say that no material gaps are known only\\n  when the evidence supports it.\\n- **Your decision:** Explain that \\\"Verify result\\\" accepts this exact candidate\\n  against the agreed requirements. Merge and release remain separate decisions.\\n- **Review details:** For PR-based work, show the confirmed PR URL prominently.\\n  Identify the exact VREC and full candidate commit. Link its governing work\\n  orders, verification contracts, assessment, and evidence at the remote review\\n  commit so the owner can read them without access to the workstation.\\n  Local-only work uses its available review locations.\\n\\nLead with ordinary language and keep the request proportionate to the work.\\nDetails may be linked, but material gaps and the decision's scope must be\\nvisible in the request. Keep passed, failed, and not-assessed results distinct.\\nAn accepted risk needs its recorded decision reference; otherwise it remains\\nunresolved. Do not silently bundle risk acceptance or waive required checks.\\n\\nOffer \\\"Verify result\\\" and \\\"Request corrections\\\" when verification is eligible.\\nIf verification is blocked, report the blocker and evaluator's next action\\ninstead of offering acceptance.\\nThe human need not type IDs or commands. Bind an unambiguous \\\"I verify\\\" or\\n\\\"Verify result\\\" to the displayed record, candidate, and evidence before applying\\nthe decision. Clarify an ambiguous reply. Reassess changed inputs under action 4;\\nsilence or implementation approval does not supply verification acceptance.\\n\\n\\\"Request corrections\\\" leaves the decision pending; it is not a terminal\\nrejection. Follow [Assess the verification evidence](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#assess-the-verification-evidence)\\nto identify the correction and eligible execution authority. A completed work\\norder does not become executable again. An explicit rejection or supersession\\nstill follows action 5 and [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision).\\n\\n**Completion:** The exact verification decision is known, or the record remains\\npending. No implementation actor infers acceptance from their own passing tests.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision) records only the selected decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"cdf0222448290088f6b56d69941badd6bd3bf0bf60c19e05ddba06b00033f081\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}]}]}\r\n",

Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 71, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected path, existing preparation authority, exact candidate,\\nand the release contract (REL) and eligible verified coverage required by that\\npath. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}]}]}\r\n",

The public reader includes the selected file's exact entry conditions when present; read their applicable references before acting. It does not follow links or select the next action.\\nFor authoring checklists and the repeated released 0.22.1 continuation heading,\\nuse the exact selectors in the selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-drafts.md`.\\n\\nFor known paths, use them directly. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Batch independent reads when their exact\\npaths are known. Unknown headings must not be guessed;\\nread the named file once to locate its actual headings. Request known current\\nsections together and reuse unchanged content. A full inventory is not required.\\n\\nRead [Execution tools](native-execution-tools.md) when choosing a planned check\\nor executing an authorized one. The description establishes the available\\nassertion and evidence fields; reading it does not run a test. Source inspection\\nis not test execution, and drafting a verification contract grants no execution\\nauthority.\\n\\n## Other operations\\n\\nRaw mode remains `remote OPERATION --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\nUse it for operations without typed input, or when explicitly checking a raw\\ncontract. Original schemas are under `reference/server/contracts/`. Selected\\nschema views use `schemas/remote-v1/OPERATION.json` or `schemas/read-v1/OPERATION.json`.\\nEach view retains its original pointer/digest. Lifecycle test-copy schemas are\\nseparate; do not load them for drafting alone. `--key` reads a receipt, not a document.\\n\\nFor lifecycle rehearsal use `remote rehearse --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record\\nABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`. The helper supplies the direct client's `--test-copy` flag;\\ndo not add that flag yourself. The request still needs `test_copy: true`.\\nThe selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-test-lifecycle.md` provides exact\\nreleased section selectors and pointers to individual action schemas.\\nFor a handoff file, `encode-file ABSOLUTE_FILE` returns its actual byte count,\\nSHA-256 and base64 content. It takes no output flag. Copy those returned values\\nunchanged; do not compute or guess a replacement digest.\\n\\nUse `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` before the final report. Read its\\nselected fields as needed. `observed_content_reads` contains successful visible\\nread metadata; `file_reads` retains Claude Read attempts, including failures.\\nUse the observed trace instead of rebuilding it with inventory lookups. Missing\\nreads remain unknown; rereading now does not prove an earlier read. The capture\\nmay be incomplete, and subsequent report writes are not yet counted. Keep the\\nrecord path as evidence instead of copying every command. This supplies no draft\\ntext, content judgement or lifecycle decision.\\n\\nThe returned `record` is the exact JSON **file**, even when it has no extension.\\nUse its `read_arguments` with the approved helper prefix. Do not append a filename\\nor treat it as a directory. Add `--pointer` only to select a field in that file.\\n\\n`command_records` includes extensionless record names. Each row points to its\\noriginal capture and copies selected exact `response_fields`, including available\\nreceipt, outcome and provenance values. Rows are sorted by filename, not time.\\nUse an indexed row to locate evidence, then inspect its original request/result\\nfor the claim. The index does not select a handoff base or certify a retry.\\n\\nRetain failed calls and recoveries. Template admission is not a content review.\\nReport only inspected facts and actual outcomes; distinguish unresolved content\\nfrom a completed definition. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}, {\"heading\": \"obtain-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Obtain the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"obtain-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 72, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"### Obtain the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The ready release record (RLS), release contract (REL), candidate,\\nverified coverage, version, and accountable human's release authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by review or the gate check.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's exact release or rejection\\n  decision, including the reason for rejection.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Present the candidate, included work, verification coverage, version,\\n   constraints, rollback conditions, and required release evidence.\\n   If the contract and delivery plan select complete release delivery, follow\\n   [Complete-release authority](AUTHORITY.md#complete-release-authority). Finish\\n   required deliverable preparation and human verification before this request.\\n   Show one concise request: \\\"Approve the complete release\\\", its versions,\\n   delivery actions, verification summary, limitations and a link to the exact\\n   plan. Include payload digests, destinations, marker targets and any bounded\\n   release-only integration in that plan.\\n2. Run the transition gate check for the intended target state.\\n3. Retain the actual human, decision reference and reviewed plan digest.\\n   Do not rewrite the plan when public observations arrive; retain them separately.\\n4. Retain a rejection reason when applicable.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `released` or `rejected` for `TARGET`, according to the proposed decision.\\nThe evaluator determines legality. A passed check does not supply approval.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is explicit, or remains pending.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required) records that decision. Execute listed delivery actions\\nunder the same complete-release authorization when their conditions still match.\\nOtherwise obtain only the exact external authority that is missing.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3f8f1bc33363c8583a4b28560220ccaa7497990299624c53d90e1b364fecca78\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h43\\\\f\\\\codex-401\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"release-coverage\", \"title\": \"Release coverage\", \"anchor\": \"release-coverage\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 148, \"content\": \"## Release coverage\\n\\nA release record (RLS) MUST bind one release contract\\n(REL), one exact candidate commit, and eligible verification records (VREC)\\nat that same commit. Governance\\nwork is included only when the release record (RLS) explicitly includes\\nverification records (VREC) that provide eligible coverage for that work.\\nA related record or dashboard cannot add work to a release.\\n\\nThis model describes the readable record structure.
